_comment: The App Store listing for Baton Music (app id 6798304294), en-US.
TWO HALVES, AND THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS:
desired -- what we intend the listing to say. Edit this. It is what
AppStoreMetadataTests checks, and what `app-store-metadata.py push`
sends to Apple the moment a version is editable.
_live   -- what App Store Connect actually held the last time this repo looked.
Written only by pull and push, never by hand. It is what makes a
hand-edit in the web form detectable: if Apple no longer matches this
snapshot, someone changed the listing outside the repo and the check
fails, which is the whole reason the file exists (TBX-5074, TBX-5075).
So `desired != _live` is a pending change waiting on a release, and `live != _live`
is drift. One is expected and one is a defect, and a mirror could not tell them apart.
python3 ios/scripts/app-store-metadata.py check   # what differs, and why
python3 ios/scripts/app-store-metadata.py push    # apply desired, where editable
Name, subtitle and keywords are only writable on a version in PREPARE_FOR_SUBMISSION.
testflight.sh pushes on every release and fails if it cannot check.
CLEAN as of 2026-09-07: the 1.1 release pushed all seven pending fields -- name,
subtitle, keywords, promotional text and the three batonmusic.app URLs -- to the 1.1
version record, re-read Apple, and rewrote _live below. That was the first time this
tool ever wrote to a real listing; it took two fixes to get there (TBX-5110, and the
release's Python 3.9).
The name is live on the version record but NOT yet in the store: Apple reviews a name,
so it changes when 1.1 is approved, not when the build uploaded (TBX-5045).
Note what _live now records: appStoreVersion 1.1, not 1.0. Until a push or pull moves
it, the version-scoped half of a snapshot describes the version named here and nothing
else -- which is why a newly created version cannot be called drift.

desired.name: Baton: Navidrome Music Player
desired.subtitle: Subsonic & OpenSubsonic client
desired.description:
Baton plays the music you host yourself. Point it at Navidrome, or any server that speaks the Subsonic API, and your whole library is on your phone: albums, artists, genres, playlists, search, downloads for offline listening, and a music friend you can ask for something to play.

No server yet? Try it anyway. The app connects to Navidrome's public demo server in one tap, and a built-in demo library plays entirely offline.

YOUR LIBRARY
- Albums, artists, genres, folders and playlists
- Search with a memory for where you went
- Downloads for offline listening
- Likes, ratings and play history that stay with your server

PLAYBACK
- Ten-band equalizer with presets, for the tracks you download; an experimental audio engine extends it to streamed music, and skips gapless and crossfade while it is on
- Gapless playback and crossfade, both switched on in Settings
- Lock screen controls, and AirPlay through the system player
- Widgets in six sizes, including Lock Screen and StandBy
- A Live Activity in the Dynamic Island while something is playing
- Ask Siri to play music, or resume it, without opening the app
- Sleep timer, and continue-where-you-left-off between devices

BEYOND THE LIBRARY
- Podcasts, subscribed on the server or by RSS on the phone
- Transcribe a podcast episode, and summarize it, using a host you run
- Internet radio stations, synced from your server
- Lyrics, with scroll-along timing where your files carry it
- Scrobbling to ListenBrainz and Last.fm, off until you connect an account
- A music friend you can chat with, powered by a model host you configure

MADE FOR SELF-HOSTERS
- Works with Navidrome and other Subsonic-compatible servers
- Pair with the Mac app by scanning a code; settings can follow you through your own gateway
- Clippings: audio your Mac read aloud and saved, collected through that gateway
- No accounts, no analytics, no tracking. The privacy policy fits on one page
- Open source under the MIT license. Buying the App Store build funds development

Baton needs a Navidrome or Subsonic-compatible server for your own music; the demo modes work without one.
